contracts.commit_point: The filesystem mutation would commit inside the external stdio MCP filesystem server reached through the MCPToolset connection (lines 33-40); the tool_filter blocks the effect upstream by excluding mutating tools from agent exposure at registration (lines 51-60).
contracts.declared_mechanism: MCPToolset tool_filter allowlist applied at toolset registration (lines 51-59), permitting only read_file, read_multiple_files, list_directory, directory_tree, search_files, get_file_info, and list_allowed_directories; lines 42-50 document the write-exclusion intent with an (inactive) lambda-filter alternative.
contracts.forbidden_condition: The agent invoking (or being exposed to) a mutating filesystem MCP tool — the in-source comment names write_file, edit_file, create_directory, and move_file as the write operations the agent must not perform — against the allowed directory.
pending_binding_information: Whether ADK MCPToolset enforces tool_filter at invocation time as well as at tool listing/registration time (framework source not supplied).

The full tool inventory of the stdio MCP filesystem server; its package identifier is sanitized as '@<REDACTED>' (line 38), so server-side write-tool names and directory confinement cannot be confirmed.
Whether the allowed read-only tool names (e.g., search_files) have any mutating side effects in the sanitized server implementation.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent-driven filesystem access performed via the stdio MCP filesystem server registered in the LlmAgent's tools list.
contracts.protected_resource: The directory at _allowed_path (os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), which is passed to the MCP filesystem server and named as the allowed directory in the agent instruction.
contracts.protection_obligation: The 'enterprise_assistant' LlmAgent must access the local filesystem only through the MCPToolset's read-only tool_filter allowlist, so that mutating filesystem MCP tools are never exposed to the agent. (Merged from first-phase and second-phase opinions describing the same tool_filter guard.)
scope_limits: Guard is declared only in adk/dev/mcp_stdio_server_agent/agent.py; no claim is made about other agents' toolsets in the repository.
Lines 43-50 are commented-out alternative wording (lambda filter naming the four write tools); they document intent but are not executed.
Deny-by-default semantics of an allowlist-style tool_filter are an ADK framework property; the framework implementation is not in supplied source.
The instruction text telling the model the allowed directory (lines 27-31) is advisory prompt content, not the declared guard mechanism.

contracts.commit_point: cursor.execute(sql_query, params) inside execute_sql (sqlite_agent.py lines 155-159), with the PermissionError guard raising at lines 151-153 before it; the connection context manager commits successful writes on exit (lines 160-166).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Default-deny flag: SQLiteAgent.__init__(write_access=False) stored as self.allow_writes (lines 27-42); _WRITE_OPERATIONS regex classification via _is_write_query (lines 22-25, 74-76); execute_sql raises PermissionError when is_write and not allow_writes, before cursor.execute (lines 149-153); siculo agent wires ALLOW_WRITES = getenv_boolean('SICULO_AGENT_ALLOW_WRITES', False) into the singleton (agent.py lines 66, 71); CLI exposes opt-in --allow-writes (main.py lines 24, 55-56).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A SQL statement matching the _WRITE_OPERATIONS prefix regex (INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|CREATE|DROP|ALTER|REPLACE) being executed while self.allow_writes is False.
pending_binding_information: Runtime value of SICULO_AGENT_ALLOW_WRITES (and CLI --allow-writes usage) in actual deployments; the source default is False.
Whether the PermissionError raised inside the ADK tool call is surfaced back to the model or aborts the agent run (ADK tool error propagation not in supplied source).
Whether any deployment constructs SQLiteAgent with write_access=True behind an agent-registered tool.
contracts.protected_operation: Generic SQL execution against the instance's SQLite database, reached from the agent via tool_execute_sql -> SingletonAgent.execute_sql (and directly via execute_sql in the CLI).
contracts.protected_resource: The SQLite database file configured per instance (DB_FILE / SICULO_AGENT_DB_FILE, default 'agents/siculo/google_events.sqlite'; args.db_file for the CLI).
contracts.protection_obligation: SQLiteAgent.execute_sql must refuse SQL write statements (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/DROP/ALTER/REPLACE) against the configured SQLite database unless write_access is explicitly enabled, raising PermissionError before execution; the production siculo agent binds this guarded executor as its SQL tool with write access defaulting to disabled. (Merged from first-phase and second-phase opinions describing the same default-deny write guard.)
scope_limits: Write classification is a statement-start regex enumerating only INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, ALTER, REPLACE; any statement-initial keyword outside that set is classified as a read (lines 22-25, 74-76, 149-151). Behavior for multi-statement strings, leading comments, or other mutating statement forms is not addressed in supplied source.

The natural-language path execute_natural_language_query is a simulated LLM placeholder in supplied source and is not registered as an agent tool in siculo/agent.py; when used (CLI exec-nl) it relies on the same execute_sql guard (sqlite_agent.py line 315).
Read operations (list_tables, get_table_schema, schema dumps, row counts) are not restricted by this obligation.

The same guard fronts the non-agent CLI path (main.py exec-sql), which is ordinary programmatic invocation rather than agent tool dispatch; the agent-mediated binding is established via siculo/agent.py.
